name: Dione
tagline: Saturn's wispy ice moon — bright fractured cliffs trailing across an ancient cratered face.
history: Dione's trailing hemisphere is veiled in bright wispy streaks — networks of fractured ice cliffs, not frost deposits as once thought. Two tiny trojan moons, Helene and Polydeuces, share its orbit at the Lagrange points. Cassini's magnetometer suggested a weak induced field, hinting at a possible buried ocean; the moon is more interesting inside than its battered face suggests.
